text: Axillary lump/swelling: A presenting complaint characterised by axillary lump/swelling.
Breast lump: A breast mass, also known as a breast lump, is a localized swelling that feels different from the surrounding tissue. Breast pain, nipple discharge, or skin changes may be present.

Breast pain: Breast pain is the symptom of discomfort in either one or both breasts. Pain in both breasts is often described as breast tenderness, is usually associated with the menstrual period and is not serious.
Nipple changes: A presenting complaint characterised by nipple changes.
Nipple discharge: Nipple discharge is fluid from the nipple, with or without squeezing the breast. The discharge can be milky, clear, green, purulent, bloody, or faintly yellow.

Abscess of breast associated with lactation: An acute infection of the breast tissue that occurs during lactation, presenting as a painful, swollen area with possible purulent discharge. Common presenting complaints: Breast Lump, Axillary Lump. Associated symptoms: Localized Breast Pain And Redness, Fever. Risk factors: Poor Latch, Nipple Trauma, Overfull Breasts, Diabetes. Age relevance: . Sex relevance: . Acute or chronic: .

Abscess of breast associated with lactation red flags. Red flag (RF_SEPSIS_SIGNS_MASTITIS) triggered by complaint 'BREAST_PAIN': [LLM DRAFT] Presence of systemic toxicity, high fever, tachycardia, or signs of sepsis secondary to severe lactation-associated breast abscess.. Red flag (RF_RAPIDLY_SPREADING_CELLULITIS) triggered by complaint 'BREAST_PAIN': [LLM DRAFT] Rapidly spreading erythema, skin necrosis, or significant worsening of localized inflammation despite initial management of a breast abscess..

Abscess of breast associated with lactation differential diagnosis notes. Compared to Abscess Of Breast Associated With The Puerperium: [LLM DRAFT] Occurs specifically in the postpartum period independent of active breastfeeding status. Compared to Mammary Duct Ectasia Of Right Breast: [LLM DRAFT] Presents with non-purulent nipple discharge and ductal dilation rather than acute infectious inflammation. Compared to Solitary Cyst Of Left Breast: [LLM DRAFT] Characterized by a smooth, fluid-filled mass without signs of acute inflammation, warmth, or fever.

Abscess of breast associated with pregnancy, first trimester: A localized collection of pus in breast tissue occurring during the first trimester of pregnancy, often presenting with pain, swelling, and erythema. Common presenting complaints: Breast Lump, Axillary Lump. Associated symptoms: Localized Breast Pain And Redness, Fever. Risk factors: Lactation, Nipple Trauma, Diabetes, Smoking. Age relevance: . Sex relevance: . Acute or chronic: .

Abscess of breast associated with pregnancy, first trimester red flags. Red flag (RF_SEPSIS_SECONDARY_TO_BREAST_ABSCESS_INFECTION) triggered by complaint 'BREAST_PAIN': [LLM DRAFT] Presents with severe localized breast pain accompanied by systemic signs of infection such as high fever, chills, tachycardia, or hypotension indicating potential progression to sepsis.. Red flag (RF_RAPIDLY_PROGRESSIVE_CELLULITIS_WITH_SKIN_NECROSIS) triggered by complaint 'BREAST_LUMP': [LLM DRAFT] Presents with a rapidly expanding, highly painful breast lump with surrounding skin breakdown, purplish discoloration, or signs of tissue necrosis requiring immediate surgical evaluation..

Abscess of breast associated with pregnancy, first trimester differential diagnosis notes. Compared to Abscess Of Breast Associated With Pregnancy Second Trimester: [LLM DRAFT] Presents later in gestation, typically with more pronounced physiologic breast enlargement and glandular development. Compared to Abscess Of Breast Associated With Lactation: [LLM DRAFT] Occurs exclusively post-delivery during breastfeeding rather than during early pregnancy. Compared to Solitary Cyst Of Unspecified Breast: [LLM DRAFT] Presents as a circumscribed, fluid-filled mass without localized signs of acute inflammation, erythema, or systemic infection.

Abscess of breast associated with pregnancy, second trimester: A localized collection of pus in the breast tissue occurring during the second trimester of pregnancy, often secondary to mastitis. Common presenting complaints: Breast Lump, Axillary Lump. Associated symptoms: Localized Breast Pain And Redness, Fever. Risk factors: Pregnancy, Breastfeeding, Nipple Trauma, Diabetes. Age relevance: . Sex relevance: . Acute or chronic: .

Abscess of breast associated with pregnancy, second trimester red flags. Red flag (RF_SEPSIS_SYSTEMIC_TOXICITY) triggered by complaint 'BREAST_PAIN': [LLM DRAFT] Presence of high fever, tachycardia, altered mental status, or rapidly spreading erythema indicating systemic infection or sepsis in pregnancy.. Red flag (RF_SEVERE_AXILLARY_COMPRESSION) triggered by complaint 'AXILLARY_LUMP': [LLM DRAFT] Rapidly enlarging axillary abscess causing severe neurovascular compromise or impending skin necrosis of the arm..

Abscess of breast associated with pregnancy, second trimester differential diagnosis notes. Compared to Abscess Of Breast Associated With Pregnancy First Trimester: [LLM DRAFT] Occurs during the earlier 1-13 weeks gestational window rather than weeks 14-27. Compared to Abscess Of Breast Associated With Lactation: [LLM DRAFT] Develops during the postpartum breastfeeding period rather than during the ongoing second trimester of gestation. Compared to Abscess Of The Breast And Nipple: [LLM DRAFT] General breast and nipple abscess presentation not specifically tied to the hormonal and physiological state of the second trimester of pregnancy.

Abscess of breast associated with the puerperium: An acute infection of breast tissue occurring during the postpartum period, presenting as a painful, localized collection of pus. Common presenting complaints: Breast Lump, Axillary Lump. Associated symptoms: Localized Breast Pain And Redness, Fever. Risk factors: Breastfeeding, Nipple Trauma, Poor Milk Removal, Diabetes. Age relevance: . Sex relevance: . Acute or chronic: .

Abscess of breast associated with the puerperium red flags. Red flag (RF_SEPTIC_SHOCK_PUERPERAL_MASTITIS) triggered by complaint 'BREAST_PAIN': [LLM DRAFT] Signs of systemic toxicity or sepsis (e.g., high fever, tachycardia, hypotension, altered mental status) in the setting of severe breast pain and puerperal abscess..

Abscess of breast associated with the puerperium differential diagnosis notes. Compared to Abscess Of Breast Associated With Lactation: [LLM DRAFT] Occurs during active breastfeeding rather than the broader postpartum/puerperal period without lactation focus. Compared to Abscess Of The Breast And Nipple: [LLM DRAFT] Involves the nipple and areolar complex specifically, often presenting with subareolar duct involvement and fistulae. Compared to Mammary Duct Ectasia Of Right Breast: [LLM DRAFT] A chronic, non-bacterial inflammatory condition featuring dilated ducts and nipple discharge, rather than an acute localized purulent collection.

Abscess of the breast and nipple: A localized collection of pus within breast tissue, often presenting with pain, swelling, redness, and fever. Common presenting complaints: Breast Pain, Breast Lump, Axillary Lump. Associated symptoms: Breast Pain, Swelling And Erythema, Purulent Nipple Discharge, Fever, Nipple Ulceration. Risk factors: Breastfeeding, Nipple Trauma, Diabetes Mellitus, Immunosuppression. Age relevance: . Sex relevance: . Acute or chronic: .

Abscess of the breast and nipple red flags. Red flag (RF_SEPSIS_OR_RAPIDLY_PROGRESSIVE_SYSTEMIC_INFECTION_SECONDARY_TO_BREAST_ABSCESS) triggered by complaint 'BREAST_PAIN': [LLM DRAFT] Presenting with signs of systemic toxicity, high fever, tachycardia, hypotension, or rapidly spreading erythema.. Red flag (RF_NECROTIZING_SOFT_TISSUE_INFECTION_OF_THE_BREAST) triggered by complaint 'BREAST_LUMP': [LLM DRAFT] Presenting with skin necrosis, crepitus, severe disproportionate pain, or rapidly advancing purple/black discoloration over the lump..

Abscess of the breast and nipple differential diagnosis notes. Compared to Mammary Duct Ectasia Of Right Breast: [LLM DRAFT] Presents with non-cyclic nipple discharge and subareolar inflammation without acute localized purulent collection. Compared to Solitary Cyst Of Unspecified Breast: [LLM DRAFT] Presents as a smooth, mobile, fluid-filled mass lacking the acute local erythema, warmth, and tenderness of an infection. Compared to Lobular Carcinoma In Situ Of Unspecified Breast: [LLM DRAFT] Typically asymptomatic and found incidentally on imaging, lacking the acute pain, inflammation, and fluctuance of an abscess.

Lobular carcinoma in situ of unspecified breast: Lobular carcinoma in situ of unspecified breast is a non‑invasive breast cancer confined to the lobules, characterized by proliferation of malignant epithelial cells without stromal invasion. Common presenting complaints: Breast Pain. Associated symptoms: Early: Vague, None. Risk factors: Brca2 Mutation, Family History Breast Cancer, Hormone Replacement Therapy, Obesity. Age relevance: . Sex relevance: . Acute or chronic: .
Lobular carcinoma in situ of unspecified breast red flags. Red flag (NONE_APPLICABLE) triggered by complaint '': .

Lobular carcinoma in situ of unspecified breast differential diagnosis notes. Compared to Solitary Cyst Of Unspecified Breast: [LLM DRAFT] Presents as a fluid-filled, mobile mass that typically demonstrates benign features on ultrasound rather than the non-palpable microcalcifications or incidental findings characteristic of LCIS. Compared to Merkel Cell Carcinoma Of Skin Of Breast: [LLM DRAFT] Manifests as a rapidly growing cutaneous or subcutaneous nodule originating from the skin rather than the terminal ductulo-lobular unit. Compared to Mammary Duct Ectasia Of Right Breast: [LLM DRAFT] Presents with nipple discharge or periareolar inflammation due to dilated ducts rather than the clonal proliferation of epithelial cells confined to the lobules seen in LCIS.

Mammary duct ectasia of right breast: Mammary duct ectasia of the right breast is a benign dilation of the milk ducts causing nipple discharge, pain, and skin changes. Common presenting complaints: Nipple Discharge, Nipple Changes. Associated symptoms: Localized Breast Pain And Redness, Fever. Risk factors: Pregnancy Lactation, Hormonal Therapy, Smoking, Age. Age relevance: . Sex relevance: . Acute or chronic: .

Mammary duct ectasia of right breast red flags. Red flag (RF_ACUTE_MASTITIS) triggered by complaint 'BREAST_PAIN': [LLM DRAFT] Severe pain with redness, warmth, and fever indicating possible abscess. Red flag (RF_BLOODY_NIPPLE_DISCHARGE) triggered by complaint 'NIPPLE_DISCHARGE': [LLM DRAFT] Sudden onset of bloody discharge warranting prompt evaluation.

Mammary duct ectasia of right breast differential diagnosis notes. Compared to Solitary Cyst Of Right Breast: [LLM DRAFT] Presents as a well-circumscribed, fluid-filled mass on imaging rather than dilated, fluid-filled subareolar ducts. Compared to Abscess Of The Breast And Nipple: [LLM DRAFT] Characterized by acute localized inflammation, severe pain, erythema, and purulent discharge rather than chronic, bland periductal inflammation. Compared to Lobular Carcinoma In Situ Of Unspecified Breast: [LLM DRAFT] Typically asymptomatic and detected mammographically as microcalcifications rather than presenting with palpable subareolar masses or nipple discharge.

Merkel cell carcinoma of skin of breast: A rare, aggressive neuroendocrine skin cancer arising in the breast skin, often presenting as a rapidly growing, painless nodule. Common presenting complaints: Breast Pain. Associated symptoms: Painless Rapidly Enlarging Nodule, Bluepurple Skin Discoloration, Ulceration Or Bleeding, Regional Lymphadenopathy. Risk factors: Light Skin, Ultraviolet Light, Radiation Therapy, Arsenic, Poor Immune Function. Age relevance: . Sex relevance: . Acute or chronic: .

Merkel cell carcinoma of skin of breast red flags. Red flag (RF_RAPIDLY_ENLARGING_BREAST_LUMP) triggered by complaint 'BREAST_LUMP': [LLM DRAFT] Breast lump that increases in size rapidly over days or weeks. Red flag (RF_NIPPLE_ULCERATION_OR_BLEEDING) triggered by complaint 'NIPPLE_CHANGES': [LLM DRAFT] Nipple changes with ulceration or active bleeding.

Merkel cell carcinoma of skin of breast differential diagnosis notes. Compared to Lobular Carcinoma In Situ Of Unspecified Breast: [LLM DRAFT] Arises from the glandular breast tissue rather than the overlying skin and is typically non-invasive and clinically occult. Compared to Abscess Of The Breast And Nipple: [LLM DRAFT] Presents with acute inflammatory signs such as localized erythema, warmth, tenderness, and purulent discharge rather than a firm, painless cutaneous nodule. Compared to Mammary Duct Ectasia Of Right Breast: [LLM DRAFT] Characterized by dilated subareolar ducts often leading to nipple retraction or thick discharge rather than a primary dermal malignant neoplasm.

Solitary cyst of left breast: A benign, fluid-filled lesion confined to the left breast, presenting as a solitary, usually painless lump. Common presenting complaints: Breast Lump. Associated symptoms: Palpable Breast Lump, Breast Pain Or Tenderness, Nipple Discharge Clear Or Serous, Skin Dimpling Or Retraction. Risk factors: Hormonal Fluctuations, Age Postmenopausal, Obesity, Family History Of Breast Disease. Age relevance: . Sex relevance: . Acute or chronic: .

Solitary cyst of left breast red flags. Red flag (RF_ACUTE_BREAST_ABSCESS) triggered by complaint 'BREAST_PAIN': [LLM DRAFT] sudden severe pain with fever, redness, or swelling indicating infection. Red flag (RF_BLOODY_NIPPLE_DISCHARGE) triggered by complaint 'NIPPLE_DISCHARGE': [LLM DRAFT] sudden onset of bloody discharge from nipple.

Solitary cyst of left breast differential diagnosis notes. Compared to Solitary Cyst Of Right Breast: [LLM DRAFT] Presents as a similar benign, fluid-filled mass but is located in the contralateral breast. Compared to Lobular Carcinoma In Situ Of Unspecified Breast: [LLM DRAFT] Manifests as non-invasive neoplastic cellular proliferation rather than a benign fluid-filled cavity. Compared to Abscess Of The Breast And Nipple: [LLM DRAFT] Presents with acute inflammatory signs such as localized erythema, warmth, and purulent tenderness rather than a smooth, painless cyst.

Solitary cyst of right breast: A benign, fluid-filled cavity within the right breast tissue, often asymptomatic and discovered incidentally. Common presenting complaints: Breast Lump. Associated symptoms: Palpable Lump, Breast Pain, Nipple Discharge, Skin Dimpling. Risk factors: Hormonalfluctuations, Age, Familyhistory, Obesity. Age relevance: . Sex relevance: . Acute or chronic: .

Solitary cyst of right breast red flags. Red flag (RF_BREAST_ABSCESS_DUE_TO_CYST_INFECTION) triggered by complaint 'BREAST_PAIN': [LLM DRAFT] Severe breast pain >8/10 with fever >38°C, redness, swelling indicating abscess. Red flag (RF_AXILLARY_ABSCESS_SECONDARY_TO_CYST) triggered by complaint 'AXILLARY_LUMP': [LLM DRAFT] Rapidly enlarging axillary lump with warmth, erythema, fever >38°C.

Solitary cyst of right breast differential diagnosis notes. Compared to Solitary Cyst Of Left Breast: [LLM DRAFT] Presents identically to a right breast cyst but is located in the contralateral breast. Compared to Mammary Duct Ectasia Of Right Breast: [LLM DRAFT] Presents with nipple discharge and ductal dilation rather than a discrete fluid-filled mass. Compared to Lobular Carcinoma In Situ Of Unspecified Breast: [LLM DRAFT] Typically asymptomatic and detected on biopsy or mammography rather than presenting as a palpable fluid-filled cyst.

Solitary cyst of unspecified breast: A solitary, usually painless cystic lesion of the breast that is not associated with a specific breast structure. Common presenting complaints: Breast Lump. Associated symptoms: Palpable Breast Lump, Breast Tenderness, Nipple Discharge, Skin Dimpling. Risk factors: Hormonal Influence, Age, Obesity. Age relevance: . Sex relevance: . Acute or chronic: .

Solitary cyst of unspecified breast red flags. Red flag (RF_ACUTE_INFECTION) triggered by complaint 'AXILLARY_LUMP': [LLM DRAFT] Sudden severe pain, redness, swelling, fever, and systemic signs of infection. Red flag (RF_ACUTE_HEMORRHAGE) triggered by complaint 'BREAST_PAIN': [LLM DRAFT] Sudden severe pain with rapid swelling, pallor, tachycardia, or signs of anemia/shock..

Solitary cyst of unspecified breast differential diagnosis notes. Compared to Solitary Cyst Of Right Breast: [LLM DRAFT] Laterality specification helps differentiate the exact anatomical location compared to an unspecified breast cyst. Compared to Solitary Cyst Of Left Breast: [LLM DRAFT] Laterality specification distinguishes the exact side of the lesion from a cyst with unspecified laterality. Compared to Lobular Carcinoma In Situ Of Unspecified Breast: [LLM DRAFT] Histological malignancy rather than a benign fluid-filled cyst distinguishes this neoplastic condition.

Traumatic amputation (partial) of part of thorax, except breast, initial encounter: Partial amputation of thoracic structures (ribs, intercostal muscles, pleura) due to traumatic injury, excluding breast tissue, presenting at initial encounter. Common presenting complaints: Breast Pain. Associated symptoms: Chest Wall Pain, Hemothorax, Respiratory Distress, Hypotension. Risk factors: High Speed Motor Vehicle Collision, Falls From Height, Workplace Industrial Accidents, Gunshot Wounds To Thorax. Age relevance: . Sex relevance: . Acute or chronic: .

Traumatic amputation (partial) of part of thorax, except breast, initial encounter red flags. Red flag (RF_EXPANDING_AXILLARY_HEMATOMA) triggered by complaint 'AXILLARY_LUMP': [LLM DRAFT] Expanding axillary swelling with hypotension or active bleeding. Red flag (RF_SEVERE_BREAST_PAIN_WITH_RESPIRATORY_DISTRESS) triggered by complaint 'BREAST_PAIN': [LLM DRAFT] Severe chest wall pain with dyspnea, tachypnea, or hypoxia.

Traumatic amputation (partial) of part of thorax, except breast, initial encounter differential diagnosis notes. Compared to Merkel Cell Carcinoma Of Skin Of Breast: [LLM DRAFT] Presents as a painless, rapidly growing cutaneous nodule rather than an acute physical trauma. Compared to Abscess Of The Breast And Nipple: [LLM DRAFT] Presents with localized pain, erythema, and purulent discharge rather than acute structural tissue loss from trauma. Compared to Solitary Cyst Of Unspecified Breast: [LLM DRAFT] Presents as a fluid-filled, mobile breast mass rather than an acute open structural injury to the chest wall.
